source.title: Contextual interpretations common in the Linear A literature
source.notes: Not a single publication. These are the interpretations that most discussions of Linear A take as a starting point, each with the internal evidence for it in `basis`, which can be checked against this database (python3 -m lineara word <form>). Before citing any of them, go to the literature. J. G. Younger, Linear A Texts in phonetic transcription, was the standard free reference; its host people.ku.edu stopped resolving (checked 2026-09-20) and the texts and lexicon now circulate as PDFs on Academia.edu. For the libation formula see B. Davis (2014), Minoan Stone Vessels with Linear A Inscriptions (Aegaeum 36).

readings.basis: Stands at the end of lists before a figure that sums the entries above it. On HT 13 the integer entries 5 + 56 + 27 + 18 + 19 + 5 give KU-RO 130. The meaning comes from position and arithmetic, not from the sound value.
HT 122b ends KU-RO 65, PO-TO-KU-RO 97; face a has KU-RO 31. As the text stands 31 + 65 = 96, one short of 97. Also on HT 131b (452). Read as KU-RO with a prefix, 'total of totals'.
Accounting term: 14 of its 15 attestations are Haghia Triada tablets, often in the same list as KU-RO (HT 123+124). The sense 'owed' is inferred from position only.

readings.gloss: opening element of the libation formula; meaning unknown
readings.basis: Stands first on stone libation vessels from several peak and cave sanctuaries (Iouktas, Syme, Palaikastro, Troullos, Kophinas). The claim is about its position, not its meaning. *301 has no agreed sound value.

Follows the opening element of the formula, and resembles Greek Δίκτη, the Cretan mountain. The identification rests on that resemblance plus position; the Palaikastro forms A-DI-KI-TE(-TE) come from the Dikte region.

The most widespread element of the formula: libation vessels from several sanctuaries, plus a metal object (PL Zf 1). The alternation JA- / A- / zero is a recurring pattern in the formula. That it names a deity is inferred from its recurrence in dedications.
Recurs in the formula, usually right after JA-SA-SA-RA-ME. Variants with an extra RU (U-NA-RU-KA-NA-TI, PK Za 11) are sometimes grouped with it.
Recurs in the formula, typically before SI-RU-TE.
Recurs in the formula, typically after I-PI-NA-MA and near the end.
